findings.text: the replacing check is co-location dependent and is silent in the mode this plan's section 3 targets: deleting only the teardown restore line in a scratch copy fails the pair serially (2 errors and the tag-inventory failure, my run, matching logs/rerun-control-delete-restore.log) but the same mutant is GREEN under -n 8 (4 passed, twice). With four cases and eight workers each case lands in its own process, so no served case ever observes the previous one's 60.0 leak and the setup check never fires; a teardown check in the leaking case's own process would fire regardless of which worker runs it.

the declared negative_control_log is logs/repro-control.log at revision 7dd1e646, the deferred-write reproduction at an intermediate commit, not the delete-restore control at the reviewed head (logs/rerun-control-delete-restore.log, rev 5561c4b0) that actually exercises the shipped setup check; the declared mutation string names 'the teardown check', which no longer exists at head.

the shipped check is a setup assertion on a later case, not the teardown check the done-when names ('a teardown check then fails the server test if serve._SIGNATURE_TTL_S is not 0.0'), and the teardown assertion 7dd1e6466 added was deleted (commit 5561c4b04), against the done-when's 'No assertion is deleted'.

the teardown comment says the fixture would 'fail here if that restore did not happen' but no assertion follows the restore; the check moved to setup, so the comment describes a check that no longer exists.

the done-when requires that when the base runs do not reproduce the failure the manifest says so; the base arms did not reproduce it (logs/base-orderA-1..3.log and base-orderB-1..3.log each end '4 passed' with ttl 0.0 at every case's setup) and the manifest does not say so. The base arms are also a hybrid scratch tree: the header line reads rev=e7eca9f0 'server test file content' and base-rev-whole-tree=7dd1e646, so only the served test file is at base.

the reviewed run's five-of-five after arms (logs/fixed-orderA-1..5.log and logs/fixed-orderB-1..5.log) run at revision 7dd1e646, one commit behind the reviewed head 5561c4b0, and that commit is exactly the change under review (the check's relocation to setup), so the stored after arm is not the reviewed head; the only arms run at the reviewed head are logs/rerun-pair-orderA/orderB.log (4 passed each).

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is made to happen and the refusal is shown. In a scratch copy of the head I deleted only the teardown restore line and re-ran the pair under -p no:xdist: the second served case errors at the setup check ('_SIGNATURE_TTL_S=60.0', assert 60.0 == 0.0 at tests/test_server_listens_before_it_watches.py:159) and the tag-inventory case fails on 'refreshed_counts["invented-during-test"] == 1', reproducing the manifest's rerun-control-delete-restore.log (1 passed, 2 errors) and its pair control. Docked seven because the check is co-location dependent and is silent in the mode this plan's section 3 targets: the same deleted-restore mutant is GREEN under -n 8 (4 passed, twice) - with four cases and eight workers each case lands in its own process, so no served case ever observes the previous one's 60.0 leak and the setup check never fires. A teardown check in the leaking case's own process would fire regardless of which worker runs it, which is the property the done-when asked for and the setup check does not have. The stop() assertion (not self.thread.is_alive()) is real and unconditional, but it covers the thread, not the memo.
justifications.evidence: added_failure_count 0 and added_failure_ids [] follow from the reviewed run's own gate arms: the baseline arms logs/base-orderA-1..3.log and logs/base-orderB-1..3.log each end '4 passed' (both file orders) and the after arms logs/fixed-orderA-1..5.log and logs/fixed-orderB-1..5.log each end '4 passed', so no id moves pass->fail in either population. I reproduced the head pair myself (4 passed, both orders) and reproduced the negative control: deleting the teardown restore in a scratch copy errors the second served case at the setup check (AssertionError _SIGNATURE_TTL_S=60.0) and fails the tag-inventory case. Docked five: (a) the done-when requires that when the base runs do not reproduce the failure the manifest says so, and it does not - the base arms did not reproduce it (every base arm ends '4 passed' with ttl 0.0 at every case's setup); (b) the base arms are not a pure base run - their header line declares rev=e7eca9f0 'server test file content' while the scratch tree's whole tree is the fix-era 7dd1e646, so only the served test file is at the node base; (c) the manifest's declared negative_control_log is logs/repro-control.log at revision 7dd1e646 (the deferred-write reproduction at an intermediate commit), not the delete-restore control at the reviewed head (logs/rerun-control-delete-restore.log, rev 5561c4b0) that actually exercises the shipped setup check; (d) the reviewed run's five-of-five after arms (logs/fixed-orderA-1..5.log and logs/fixed-orderB-1..5.log) run at 7dd1e646, one commit behind the reviewed head 5561c4b0, and that commit is exactly the check's relocation to setup, so the stored after arm is not the reviewed head - the only arms at the reviewed head are logs/rerun-pair-orderA/orderB.log (4 passed each).
justifications.fit: The change follows the file's own idiom: the join and its bound (_THREAD_STOP_S) sit beside the existing bounded waits, and the setup check is a plain assert with a mechanism comment. No plan label, sprint, ticket, version or author attribution appears in the changed path, symbol or comment. Docked two: the teardown comment at tests/test_server_listens_before_it_watches.py:212-217 still says the fixture would 'fail here if that restore did not happen' but no assertion follows the restore any more (the check moved to setup), so the comment describes a check that no longer exists; and the two comments anchor a moving target - the literal line numbers 'reckon/serve.py:3399', which rot on any edit above them - rather than the assignment they name.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal - contain the served-entry-point test's discovery memo so no later test in the same process reads a live memo - is met, and I reproduced it independently in a scratch copy of the reviewed head (5561c4b0) with my own probe logging serve._SIGNATURE_TTL_S around every case: the memo reads 60.0 at each served test's teardown (the served thread's write, reckon/serve.py:3399) and 0.0 at every following case's setup, and tests/test_tag_inventory.py::test_discovery_derives_tag_inventory_from_every_resource_type starts at 0.0 and passes; the pair is 4 passed in both file orders in my runs, matching the manifest's rerun pair logs (4 passed). The mechanism is named at file and line and is correct: serve.main assigns _SIGNATURE_TTL_S on the daemon thread, so monkeypatch's undo cannot be ordered against that write. Docked three because the shipped repairing check is not the check the done-when names: the done-when requires a teardown check that fails the server test if _SIGNATURE_TTL_S is not 0.0 and states 'No assertion is deleted', and at head the teardown assertion 7dd1e6466 added is deleted (commit 5561c4b04) and replaced by a setup check on a later case, under a SPEC of 'exact - implement as written'.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 6d7d5a469 5561c4b04 lists exactly two paths - tests/test_server_listens_before_it_watches.py and its own fragment docs/evidence/fragments/the-suite-is-green-at-head/a-served-thread-leaves-no-memo-behind.html - both inside the node's declared write paths, and the node base e7eca9f03..5561c4b04 changes the same two paths only; reckon/serve.py is untouched, as the done-when requires. The executable change is confined to the test file. The worker committed locally with a conventional subject and a body, did not mutate the plan, project index or sprint state, and the reviewed worktree is clean at 5561c4b0. No write outside the granted paths.
